In [[category theory]], an abstract branch of mathematics, a '''dominant functor''' is a [[functor]] ''F''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''C''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''D'' in which every object of ''D'' is a [[Deformation retract|retract]] of an object of the form ''F''(''c'') for some object ''c'' of&nbsp;''C''.<ref>{{citation|journal=Applied Categorical Structures|date=March 2014|title=On normal tensor functors and coset decompositions for fusion categories|first1=A.|last1=Bruguières|first2=Sebastian|last2=Burciu|doi=10.1007/s10485-014-9371-x|arxiv=1210.3922}}.</ref> In other words, <math>F</math> is dominant if for every object <math>d \in D</math>, there is an object <math>c \in C</math> together with morphisms <math>r\colon  F(c) \to d</math> and <math>s\colon  d \to F(c)</math> such that <math>r\circ s=\operatorname{id}_{d}</math>.
